info.title: Distribo API
info.description: API for the Distribo delivery platform backend. Generated directly from the Zod schemas that validate each endpoint at runtime, so it always reflects the current API.

bearerAuth.description: JWT access token returned by POST /auth/login or /auth/register/verify

get.summary: Pull what changed for the signed-in person since the last pull
get.description: Returns, per synchronized table, the rows created, updated and deleted since `last_pulled_at` (epoch milliseconds; absent for a first pull), limited to what the caller may see. Order, order line and delivery rows follow the role of the caller: supplier view for owners, managers and sellers, a narrower view for drivers, the customer view for customers. The header `X-Scope-Version` is the rights version the phone knows: when it is lower than the person's and `last_pulled_at` is set, the answer is `{ resync_required: true }` without changes and the phone starts again with a full pull. A full pull records the version on the device. Every pull sets the device `last_synced_at`. `customer_prices` created/updated rows identify `product_variant_id`, never `product_id`. Clients must migrate their local price references to variants; there is no legacy field alias. Rights scope versions and incremental timestamp/deletion rules are unchanged.

schema.description: Epoch milliseconds of the previous pull
The rights version the phone knows; absent counts as 0

200.description: The changes per table and the timestamp to send as the next `last_pulled_at`

401.description: Missing or invalid token, or `SESSION_REVOKED` for a revoked device

404.description: Not found

post.summary: Push what the phone did offline
post.description: Body `{ changes: { <table>: { created, updated, deleted } } }`, at most 2000 rows in total (body limit 5 MB). The batch is archived as received first. Then: an `X-App-Version` below the platform minimum gets 426 `APP_UPDATE_REQUIRED`; an `X-Client-Time` more than 5 minutes from server time sets `clock_skew`; an updated row changed on the server after `last_pulled_at` gets 409 `SYNC_CONFLICT` and nothing is applied; otherwise the batch is judged in one transaction. A table the server does not know is counted in `aside` and the rest passes. A processed push sets the device's `last_synced_at`.

schema.description: Epoch milliseconds of the previous pull
Phone clock, epoch milliseconds or ISO 8601

200.description: The batch was processed

400.description: Invalid query, headers or body, or more than 2000 rows

401.description: Missing or invalid token, or `SESSION_REVOKED` for a revoked device

404.description: Not found

409.description: `SYNC_CONFLICT`: pull the latest changes, then send again

426.description: `APP_UPDATE_REQUIRED`: the app version is below the platform minimum

get.summary: List the orders and deliveries the server flagged for the caller to resolve
get.description: Orders and deliveries whose `sync_issue` is not empty and that the caller entered, delivered or is assigned to; an OWNER sees all of the organization. `code` is the text before the first colon of the issue and `message` the issue text. Newest first, paginated; an issue disappears when the record is corrected. A delivery is dated by its order.

get.description: Orders of the organization created in the period whose `sync_issue` is not empty, counted per code. `PRICE_CHANGED` carries the francs lost on lines sold below the current price, `CREDIT_EXCEEDED` the amount over the limit; other codes have amount 0. Same period rules as the money exceptions: `from` and `to` as dates, default the last 7 days, at most 92 days apart.

post.summary: Replay an archived batch after the cause of a refusal is fixed (super administrator only)
post.description: The batch is judged as if sent by its author with their current rights, never the administrator's: only the version, clock and conflict checks of a push are skipped. A REPLAY_SYNC journal row (archive id and reason) is written in the same transaction, and the author and the owners get a notification. A batch can be replayed more than once; lines are idempotent by record id.
